newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela Aug non-oil exports up 20 pct vs yr ago.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela Aug non-oil exports up 20 pct vs yr ago.

text.p: Venezuela's non-traditional exports, which exclude oil and iron, were up 20.1 percent in August from a year earlier, to $430 million from $358 million, the Central Office of Statistics and Information (OCEI) said on Wednesday.
August exports were up $105 million, or 32.3 percent, from July's $325 million, OCEI figures showed.
Exports for the first eight months of the year were down 12.8 percent from a year earlier, to $2.661 billion from $3.051 billion.
Non-traditional exports rose about four percent in 1995.

"Common metals" was the strongest export sector in the first eight months of 1996, at 38.8 percent of total exports. "Chemical products" came next at 13.5 percent, then "transport materials" at 9.9 percent.

Colombia was the chief market for Venezuela's non-traditional exports with 27.6 percent. The next largest export market was the U.S. with a 23.6 percent, followed by the Netherlands with 5.2 percent and Japan with 2.5 percent.
